item.title: No guarantee Nawaqanitawase will return to Wallabies, agent says
item.description: Code-hopping winger Mark Nawaqanitawase will not play for Australia in the Nations Championship in November and might consider representing Fiji or Italy at next year's Rugby World Cup, his agent told News Corp on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Code-hopping winger Mark Nawaqanitawase will not play for Australia in the Nations Championship in November and might consider representing Fiji or Italy at next year's Rugby World Cup, his agent told News Corp on Tuesday. Nawaqanitawase played 11 tests for the Wallabies and took part in the Paris Olympics for the Australia Sevens team before switching to rugby league with the Sydney Roosters in 2024. He was always committed to returning to rugby union despite enjoying huge success in the 13-man code, representing Australia and New South Wales before finishing up by [USN:L4N45Q016 TEXT:"winning"] the National Rugby League (NRL) title with the Roosters earlier this month. The 26-year-old is contracted to Japan's Wild Knights for two years and will become eligible to play for Fiji and Italy next season through paternal and maternal heritage respectively. "Mark will not be available for international rugby this year," his agent Milan Volavola-Shankar told News Corp's Code Sports on Tuesday. "As of August next year, Mark will have completed his three-year international stand-down period. With his heritage making him eligible to represent both Italy and Fiji, he remains open to all options regarding his international future. "At this stage, Mark’s priority is establishing himself in Japan and continuing to develop his rugby, with any future international decisions to be considered at the appropriate time." Australia will play England, Scotland and Wales in the Nations Championship in November and host the World Cup next year.

item.title: BP sees 60% refining margin jump, debt fall, but flags more impairments
item.description: BP estimated on Tuesday its refining margins jumped nearly 60% in the third quarter as the Iran war boosts profits for oil majors, but also flagged $3 billion to $4.5 billion in impairments relating to its gas and low-carbon energy segment.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly, Shadia Nasralla
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) estimated on Tuesday its refining margins jumped nearly 60% in the third quarter as the Iran war boosts profits for oil majors, but also flagged $3 billion to $4.5 billion in impairments relating to its gas and low-carbon energy segment. This is the second time in a year that the British firm has booked large write-downs in its low-carbon business after [USN:L6N3YF0FC TEXT:"writing down"] over $4 billion related to its solar, biogas and offshore wind businesses as the main reasons. The group declined to provide details of the latest impairments. BP estimated its refining indicator margin for the July-September quarter at $46.7 per barrel, up from $29.6 per barrel in the second quarter and $15.8 per barrel a year ago. The Iran war has disrupted global oil supplies, driving up prices and oil majors' margins. A boost to refining margins will lift BP's profit in the products segments by $1.9 billion to $2.1 billion compared with the previous quarter, the group said in a trading statement ahead of results due on October 30. BP in recent years has changed its methodology for calculating refining margins, making historic comparisons difficult. Rival Shell (SHEL.L) said last week it [USN:L4N45T0DM TEXT:"expected "]its third-quarter refining margin to jump to $42 a barrel, a record high and sharply above $24 a barrel in the previous quarter. BP expects its third-quarter gas marketing and trading result to significantly exceed that from the previous quarter. The oil trading result is expected to be broadly flat compared with the second quarter, in what has been a strong year in trading for its oil desk. NET DEBT TARGET HIT Helped by a pause in its [USN:L6N3Z60EQ TEXT:"buyback programme"] this year, high prices and asset sales, BP expects its net debt to stand at between $13.5 billion and $14.4 billion in the third quarter, hitting its target of between $14 billion to $18 billion about a year early. Together with hybrid bonds, leases and its Deepwater Horizon oil spill liabilities, BP estimated its overall obligations at between $43.6 billion and $44.6 billion in the third quarter, down from $53.6 billion in the previous three months. This does not include its $6 billion sale of a stake in its Castrol lubricants business. BP put its upstream production at 2.19 million to 2.24 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, compared with 2.2 million in the previous quarter. The firm will provide a strategy and outlook update on December 15 in New York, which will "set out the next phase of delivering a simpler, stronger and more valuable BP," a spokesperson said.

item.title: El capital riesgo repunta en América Latina, pero menos "startups" logran despegar, según informe
item.description: La inversión en empresas emergentes en América Latina aumentó notablemente en 2025, pero la recuperación está llegando a menos empresas y haciendo menos para ayudar a las empresas más pequeñas a convertirse en grandes compañías, según un informe publicado el martes por la consultora Endeavor y la firma de inversión Glisco Partners.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: La inversión en empresas emergentes en América Latina aumentó notablemente en 2025, pero la recuperación está llegando a menos empresas y haciendo menos para ayudar a las empresas más pequeñas a convertirse en grandes compañías, según un informe publicado el martes por la consultora Endeavor y la firma de inversión Glisco Partners. Las empresas emergentes de la región captaron 4.700 millones de dólares en 2025, un 65% más que en 2024. Sin embargo, el número de rondas de financiación seguía muy por debajo del máximo del mercado, con 554 operaciones frente a las 788 de 2022. "El capital está regresando a LATAM, pero la pregunta más importante ya no es cuánto dinero entra: es cuántas compañías logran escalar. La recuperación es real, aunque todavía es parcial", dijo Alfredo Castellanos, socio director de Glisco Partners. Muchas de las mayores rondas de financiación se concentraron en empresas más conocidas que ya han alcanzado un tamaño considerable, entre ellas la mexicana de pagos digitales Clip, la plataforma de compraventa de automóviles usados por internet Kavak, la aplicación financiera argentina Ualá y la empresa mexicana de tecnología financiera Plata, indicó el informe. Las empresas emergentes en sus etapas más tempranas concentraron el 56% de todas las operaciones en 2025, pero recibieron apenas el 7% de la financiación total. También parece reducirse el número de empresas que avanzan hacia etapas posteriores. De las que captaron capital semilla en 2022, sólo el 5% había alcanzado la siguiente gran etapa de financiación al llegar al cuarto año. La inteligencia artificial atrajo más dinero, incluso en un mercado más débil. La financiación de empresas que utilizan IA aumentó a 327 millones de dólares en el primer semestre de 2026, frente a los 165 millones del mismo periodo del año anterior. Kavak utiliza ahora un agente de IA que ejerce de "director ejecutivo" para gestionar aspectos logísticos, como el inventario, comenzando por sus operaciones en la ciudad mexicana de Cuernavaca, dijo el director de producto, Alejandro Maza. Añadió que estas herramientas podrían utilizarse para duplicar las ganancias de aquí a finales de año.

item.content:encoded: French supermarket chain Co-Operative U had 80 of its stores - out of an overall group total of 2,000 - affected by this week's [USN:L8N45Y11U TEXT:"cyberattack"], said company head Dominique Schelcher on Tuesday. "It affected a minority of our stores," he told RTL radio. item.title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement leaders demanding election chief's resignation
item.description: Top leaders of the movement were detained after they jumped barricades to enter the grounds of the Jantar Mantar observatory popular for protests, chanting slogans demanding the chief election commissioner's resignation over a controversial revision of voter lists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top leaders of India's "cockroach" youth movement were detained on Tuesday after they jumped barricades to enter the grounds of a historic observatory popular for protests, chanting slogans demanding the chief election commissioner's resignation over a controversial [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists."] Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition groups have held almost daily protests this month to demand commissioner [USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:"Gyanesh"][USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:" Kumar's"] resignation over the revisions critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Thousands joined a [USN:L6N45Y06O TEXT:"protest march by opposition groups"] on Monday, after a clampdown foiled CJP plans for a weekend demonstration, with police detaining thousands of protesters, including CJP leaders. Delhi Police announced on Monday that the Jantar Mantar open air observatory, in the national capital's central business district, was no longer designated as an official protest site, and said three new venues had been identified. The CJP said its leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, and Ajinkya Shinde were among about 20 volunteers who "sneaked" inside the observatory to "reclaim" it and were detained. "You cannot denotify the resistance," founder Abhijeet Dipke said on X after their detention. BIGGEST POLITICAL CHALLENGE FOR MODI A CJP livestream showed about a dozen volunteers jumping a gate and barricades to reach the site, where they waved the Indian flag and chanted slogans before police detained them. Delhi Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The youth movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs, is among the biggest political challenges to Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power. A [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"weeks-long sit-in"] by its supporters at Jantar Mantar earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks. The latest protests erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported last month that Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems. The change, which started last year, removed over 130 million names – more than the population of Japan – from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party — allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

item.title: South Korea to relocate about 10,000 government jobs to Sejong from Seoul by 2031
item.description: South Korea will relocate about 10,000 government jobs and 44 central government agencies from the Seoul metropolitan area to Sejong city between 2027 and 2031, the interior ministry said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea will relocate about 10,000 government jobs and 44 central government agencies from the Seoul metropolitan area to Sejong city between 2027 and 2031, the interior ministry said on Tuesday. Here are some details: A total of 44 agencies and 9,929 government employees will be relocated from the capital region to the country's administrative city of Sejong, a ministry press release said. Twenty-seven agencies, representing 2,995 jobs, will move in 2027 using leased office space in Sejong. Early movers include the Financial Services Commission, Personal Information Protection Commission, Nuclear Safety and Security Commission, National Human Rights Commission and Overseas Koreans Agency. Seventeen agencies requiring dedicated facilities will relocate after new government buildings are constructed, with moves completed by 2031. Those agencies include the foreign, unification and defence ministries, the National Police Agency, Board of Audit and Inspection, Corruption Investigation Office and newly established prosecution and serious crime investigation bodies. The government estimates about 3.1 trillion won ($2.3 billion) will be needed to construct new office complexes, while 89.7 billion won will be spent on leased facilities and relocation support. The government plans to seek legislative changes to remove exemptions that currently prevent the foreign, unification, defence, justice and gender equality ministries from relocating. A [USN:L4N44V054 TEXT:"presidential office"] in Sejong is due for completion in 2029, while a Sejong branch of parliament is scheduled to open in 2033. The government has previously said the move to Sejong, which is about 110 km (68.35 miles) south of Seoul, is part of a broader strategy to tackle the concentration of population, capital, businesses and infrastructure in the capital region, while other parts of the country confront demographic decline.( $1 = 1344.4 won )

item.title: Eight people hurt in supermarket stabbing in South Korea's Incheon, police say
item.description: Eight people were wounded in a stabbing at a supermarket in the South Korean city of Incheon on Tuesday, with one person suffering cardiac arrest, police said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eight people were wounded in a stabbing at a supermarket in the South Korean city of Incheon on Tuesday, with one person suffering cardiac arrest, police said. Officers responding to the scene arrested a male suspect and were investigating the motive and circumstances of the attack, a police spokesperson said by telephone. A witness cited by Yonhap News Agency said the suspect appeared to have knives tethered to both hands and moved through several floors of the shopping complex, attacking people as he went before being subdued by bystanders and handed over to police. South Korean media reports described the suspect as a man in his 60s who was wearing an electronic monitoring ankle bracelet. The victims included six women and two men, with a woman in her 20s in cardiac arrest, the reports said. Incheon, west of Seoul, is home to South Korea's main airport and forms part of the wider Seoul metropolitan area. South Korea was shaken by a series of stabbing rampages in 2023, including attacks that left multiple people dead and injured. More recently in May, a 17-year-old girl was fatally stabbed and another teenager hurt in the southwestern city of Gwangju by a man in his 20s, who was later sentenced by a court to life in prison.

item.title: Drone sinks ship off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, prime minister says
item.description: Two ships were hit by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one of them sank, in the second such incident in a week, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two ships were hit by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one of them sank, in the second such incident in a week, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said on Tuesday. The Ukrainian-owned "Chelsea 3", sailing under Maltese flag, was hit by three drones and damaged some 18 nautical miles (33 km) off the Bulgaria coast around 1:30 a.m. (2230 GMT), Radev said. Its crew - seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis - had been rescued. Five crew members received medical assistance, but no one was seriously injured. One crew member of the sunken ship had also been rescued, Radev said. "This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters," Radev said in a televised address. "I am due to speak with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte." Radev said there was no clear evidence who carried out the attack but "the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", adding that he would summon the Russian ambassador about the incident. Bulgaria does not border either Ukraine or Russia, but as a NATO member it holds a strategic position on the Black Sea, where both countries have major ports. There are growing concerns about hybrid attacks involving drones by Russia as it wages war in Ukraine. (This story has been corrected to remove 'Ukrainian-owned' from the headline, and to clarify that the Ukrainian ship was damaged, not sunk, in paragraph 2.)

item.title: Banking watchdogs ramp up AI scrutiny as stability fears mount, sources say
item.description: Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, six people familiar with the matter said, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability.
item.dc:creator: Nupur Anand, Phoebe Seers, Tommy Wilkes
item.content:encoded: Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, six people familiar with the matter said, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability. The regulatory scrutiny, fresh details of which are reported here for the first time, reflects growing recognition that advances in frontier AI may require costly investments in cyber recovery, greater attention to dependencies on external technology providers and in some jurisdictions more formal regulatory guidance, sources said. Three top regulators in the United States, including the Federal Reserve, are quizzing banks about their use of advanced artificial intelligence models, two of the people told Reuters, [USN:L4N42A1E4 TEXT:"which adds to prior scrutiny"]. Questions include whether they deploy Chinese-developed technology, use AI agents in cyber defence and can control increasingly autonomous systems, three of the people said. In Europe, supervisors including the Bank of England and the European Central Bank are pressing banks to improve recovery plans, concerned that rapid advances in AI could cause serious harm and disruption in financial markets sooner than previously feared, three people with knowledge of their thinking said. A senior executive at a large European bank said they too are worried about potentially major damage to banking and financial markets within six months. The debate over AI oversight has intensified amid warnings from the industry after recent incidents, with JPMorgan (JPM.N) CEO Jamie Dimon urging corporate leaders to join a US-focused industry group to address AI risks, [USN:L1N4421O4 TEXT:"Reuters reported"]. US cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said this month a person in China likely used a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code [USN:L1N45T11Q TEXT:"in a hack"] on South Korean banks. Rogue AI agents developed by OpenAI were meanwhile involved in a breach of AI platform Hugging Face, [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"Reuters reported"]. Anthropic researchers have warned that increasingly powerful AI systems could eventually escape human control and even pose an existential threat, prompting calls [USN:L6N4520JA TEXT:"for stricter regulation"]. The International Monetary Fund [USN:L6N45Y0TS TEXT:"warned"] on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing various risks including the potential for a cyberattack. The IMF said a major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence, and it called on policymakers to boost cybersecurity capacity. Banks are competing to adopt [USN:L4N432191 TEXT:"agentic AI"], which can accomplish tasks with minimal human supervision, while also grappling with the challenges of new models including IT weaknesses flagged by Anthropic's [USN:L6N41J114 TEXT:"Mythos"] tool. "The adoption of AI is often outpacing the ability to put the controls in place," said Michael Woodbridge, London-based cybersecurity partner at Grant Thornton. US CONCERNS AIM AT AGENTIC AI The US regulatory inquiries centre on how banks use agentic AI in areas such as cybersecurity, focusing on whether AI agents are being used to identify, prioritize and respond to threats. Questions from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Fed focus on what limits are placed on systems, how their actions are monitored and approved and whether banks can clearly track and audit AI agent decisions, two of the people said. They are also asking what safeguards exist to prevent agents from exceeding their authority, whether humans remain involved in key decisions and how banks can shut down autonomous systems. The OCC, the Fed and the FDIC declined to comment. Through their questions, regulators are probing more specific issues tied to advanced AI models, including the use of autonomous AI agents, foreign-developed models and new cyber risks, the three people with knowledge of their thinking said. The written and verbal inquiries to large, mid-size and smaller banks show regulators are focusing on vulnerabilities from banks' use of AI and their preparedness to act, they added. Regulators are still gathering information and are not yet being prescriptive about what lenders should be doing, they said. EUROPEANS WORRY ABOUT RECOVERY Supervisors in Britain are separately encouraging the largest banks to examine so-called bare metal recovery plans, two of the people familiar with their thinking said. These systems are entirely independent from a bank's main tech set-up and can kick in if primary operating systems are compromised. Building and maintaining such state-of-the-art recovery is expensive, however, the people said. Rather than introduce new requirements, UK authorities intend to work collaboratively with industry, they added. The BoE declined to comment. The ECB in July gave lenders an end-October deadline to [USN:L8N4390I3 TEXT:"produce plans to counter AI-enabled cyber threats"], including improved back-up and recovery. Asked about its strategy for regulating AI, the ECB referred to its July letter as well as a June speech by board member Frank Elderson who stressed the need to create a sense of urgency, not alarm, about the threats. The need for supervisory action has taken on added urgency after European banks and regulators [USN:L6N4130SI TEXT:"expressed frustration"] at getting limited access to Mythos this year, amid concerns US banks will be given first sight to test frontier models. Like their US counterparts, UK supervisors are also asking banks to use frontier AI to identify vulnerabilities and accelerate patching, two people said, with one adding that lenders were so far doing a good job. The third person said euro zone banks were also being asked to map how AI is being used across their businesses and third-party providers, to understand key dependencies and ensure they can switch off and restart systems in a controlled manner. Significant gaps remained at some firms, they added. "To protect against attacks, rapid recovery matters as much as prevention," said Sukand Ramachandran, managing director and senior partner at BCG. Without separately held clean, secure copies of critical data, "a serious attack could lock customers out of their accounts and disrupt payments across the wider economy", Ramachandran told Reuters.

item.title: Europe's carmakers turn back time to rival Chinese EVs
item.description: As Chinese electric vehicle makers challenge Europe's auto industry with cheaper cars and increasingly sophisticated technology, established automakers are fighting back with one asset their rivals lack: history.
item.dc:creator: Gilles Guillaume, Rachel More
item.content:encoded: As Chinese electric vehicle makers challenge Europe's auto industry with cheaper cars and increasingly sophisticated technology, established automakers are fighting back with one asset their rivals lack: history. Europe's carmakers are increasingly reviving classic models from past decades, from Renault's 5 to Citroen's 2CV, betting nostalgia can help them stand out from a growing wave of Chinese rivals and win over EV buyers. The stakes are high. Demand for EVs has [USN:L8N45O0IP TEXT:"surged"] in Europe alongside soaring fuel prices, but Chinese manufacturers including BYD (002594.SZ) and Geely already had almost 11% of the European market in the second quarter, according to Schmidt Automotive Research, with models that are often cheaper and boast more advanced technology than local brands. While European automakers race to cut costs and narrow the technology gap, heritage is emerging as one of the few advantages China's newer entrants cannot readily replicate. The strategy has already paid off for France's Renault (RENA.PA) . The new electric version of the Renault 5, first launched in 1972, is the best-selling mid-sized EV in Europe so far this year, helping lift the group's first-half [USN:L1N43V11N TEXT:"revenue"] 9%. Now others are in pursuit. Stellantis (STLAM.MI) unveiled an electric version of Citroen's iconic 2CV, produced from 1948 to 1990, at this week's [USN:L1N45S104 TEXT:"Paris Autoshow"], while Volkswagen's electric Polo borrows heavily from the 1980s golden era of the Golf. "We're looking to differentiate ourselves and also to evoke a certain emotional response," said Renault Group design chief Laurens van den Acker. ANYTHING TO ADD VALUE For some buyers, the strategy appears to be working. Briton Chris Litchfield, 51, bought an EV for the first time in May after growing up with Renault 5s and opting for a yellow electric version of the car. "The impulse to have a new Renault 5 was far greater than my reservations about having an EV," he said. "The main reason I love it is that it's a Renault 5." "It's an absolute refreshed, modern reimagining of it." Volkswagen's ID. Polo, part of a suite of affordable EVs designed to fend off Chinese rivals, has triggered a similar response, with an optional retro dashboard mode that mimics the classic speedometer of an early Golf and plays music on a virtual cassette tape. "We only meant it as a joke," Volkswagen's chief designer Andreas Mindt said of the opt-in feature. But "people love it". Stellantis (STLAM.MI) is hoping for similar success with the new electric 2CV, targeting die-hard fans of the compact car while appealing to a broader audience seeking an affordable EV. "It's notable that we're seeing this kind of retro thing in small affordable EVs in Europe," said Robert Dooley, senior design strategist at Car Design Research, "because that's where the price pressure from Chinese brands is going to be strongest." With low margins for small cars, "anything you can do to add a little bit more value is going to be well received," he added. RELYING ON HISTORY HAS LIMITS The strategy has its limitations, however. While going retro has potential in Europe, where families often remained loyal to particular models and designs for generations, it may not work elsewhere, nor indefinitely, Van den Acker said. "Icons are not eternal, they have their moment in the sun," he said, adding that automakers need to identify the right opportunity because one generation's icon may be replaced by another's. Some earlier attempts have had limited success. Strong initial interest in Volkswagen's ID. Buzz electric microbus earlier this decade faded as US consumers balked at its price and driving range. The Beetle, a classic 20th-century design that transcended its Nazi-era origins through 1960s counterculture, never made it into the EV era. Volkswagen discontinued it in 2019 as consumer tastes shifted towards SUVs. "We should not rest on our history," said Volkswagen's Mindt, stressing the importance of features such as fast charging and autonomous driving. "We should excel in the technologies we need for the future." There is also the risk of disappointing fans. Ahead of the electric 2CV's launch, Citroen sought input from collectors of the original model on what should be retained. Respondents highlighted its affordability, ease of driving and trademark soft top. But for Thierry Jouanny, head of a French 2CV collectors' club, and proud owner of a 1951 model, any revival must also capture the emotional appeal of the original. "The new 2CV needs to have that certain something that's hard to put into words," he said. "That element that attracts people, so you are no longer an anonymous person blending into the crowd."

item.title: Blackstone-backed AirTrunk delays Singapore REIT IPO amid AI stock selloff, sources say
item.description: Blackstone -backed data-center operator AirTrunk has postponed a planned Singapore REIT IPO that could raise about $1.5 billion, two people with direct knowledge of the matter said, as a tech and AI stock selloff rattles markets.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Kane Wu
item.content:encoded: Blackstone (BX.N) -backed data-center operator AirTrunk has postponed a planned Singapore REIT IPO that could raise about $1.5 billion, two people with direct knowledge of the matter said, as a tech and AI stock selloff rattles markets. AirTrunk was originally planning to launch the IPO in [USN:L4N43H0OM TEXT:"September or October"] but put it on hold due to market conditions, said the people, declining to be named as the information was confidential. AirTrunk has not decided when to launch the offering but is aiming to complete the listing by early next year, one of them said. The delay comes as [USN:L1N45Z029 TEXT:"Asian equities slid"] to more than two-month lows on Tuesday, led by a rout in chipmakers that renewed investor scrutiny of the AI trade. AirTrunk, which is owned by US investment firm Blackstone, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Blackstone declined to comment. The Wall Street Journal [USN:FWN45Y2TF TEXT:"first reported"] the delay on Tuesday. The REIT was expected to be valued at about $15 billion, potentially making it one of Southeast Asia's largest listings in coming months. The postponement also follows the [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"scrapping of Firmus' planned IPO"], highlighting an increasingly difficult backdrop for large data centre and AI-linked equity offerings as investors reassess valuations, rising borrowing costs and the durability of demand tied to the AI boom. Singapore-based data center operator [USN:L4N45R1CS TEXT:"DayOne is aiming to launch its US"] IPO before the midterm election, Reuters reported in September.

item.title: Visa gets approval to prepare for domestic business in China
item.description: US payments firm Visa has received approval from China's central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world's largest payment markets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US payments firm Visa (V.N) has received approval from China's central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world's largest payment markets. The move marks a major step for Visa to join rivals American Express (AXP.N) and Mastercard (MA.N) in operating bank card clearing services in China and represents a further opening up of the nation's tightly controlled financial sector. The People's Bank of China (PBOC) issued an administrative approval to Visa Information Technology (Beijing) Co Ltd permitting it to begin preparatory work, according to the central bank's website. Visa Information Technology (Beijing) is a foreign-invested enterprise established in China by Visa. "The approval of our Application to Prepare marks a significant step forward in Visa's long-standing commitment to China," Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said in a statement on Tuesday. The approval comes after US President Donald Trump's [USN:L8N41P04S TEXT:"summit"] with Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier this year in China, which included more than a dozen CEOs of top US companies, including those of Mastercard and Visa. "We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world's largest economies," McInerney said. Visa must complete its preparations within one year, after which it can apply to open for business, the PBOC said. The central bank, together with the nation's top banking regulator, will review the application and, if it approves, issue a bank card clearing business license. A GOODWILL GESTURE? Visa was hoping to break into the Chinese market, which is dominated by state-controlled China UnionPay, with an unprecedented 100% ownership stake in a future joint venture license, sources have told Reuters. "This should be viewed as a goodwill gesture from Beijing towards Washington ahead of the next meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump," said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group. The two are expected to meet again on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in November. Greater market access in financial services has long been a priority for Washington, which has consistently urged Beijing to provide a more open and level playing field for foreign firms operating in China's financial sector, said Chen. Mastercard, partnering with local clearinghouse NetsUnion Clearing Corp, won approval to prepare to set up its bank card clearing business in China in 2020. American Express' joint venture in the country was cleared to start bank card clearing services later that year. In China, bank cards processed 4.6 trillion transactions worth 963.60 trillion yuan ($143.92 trillion) in 2025, according to data from the central bank, highlighting the market's enormous potential.

item.title: India's tough FX measures rattle banks, trigger unintended consequences
item.description: A series of tough regulatory steps by the Indian central bank, aimed at supporting the rupee, is leading to unintended consequences, with several lenders holding back on quoting dollar-rupee forwards, according to eight bankers.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora, Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: A series of tough regulatory steps by the Indian central bank, aimed at supporting the rupee, is leading to unintended consequences, with several lenders holding back on quoting dollar-rupee forwards, according to eight bankers. The measures and a heightened scrutiny of dollar purchases have led to uncertainty about the scope of the new rules and whether more curbs may be in the offing, the bankers said. Since Saturday, the RBI has rerouted oil dollar demand to a special facility, [USN:L1N45W00Y TEXT:"imposed a cash margin"] for derivatives used to hedge some merchant transactions and subsequently [USN:L4N45Z04K TEXT:"extended the margin"] to banks hedging their own assets and liabilities. The RBI has also told banks to offer non-deliverable contracts to clients only for protecting underlying exposures. The curbs followed a drop in the rupee to near record lows of 96.96 against the dollar last week, despite the central bank raising interest rates for the first time in nearly four years. After the measures, the currency has recovered to 95.25. "The Reserve Bank of India has moved from signalling that the rupee’s weakness may be excessive to directly restraining dollar demand and speculative activity in the FX market," said Mitul Kotecha, head of FX & EM macro strategy Asia at Barclays. "Such measures can influence the timing, venue and cost of dollar demand, but they cannot eliminate genuine demand generated by trade, hedging requirements or capital outflows," he said. The RBI did not respond to an email seeking comment on its moves and the market reaction. UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCES On Tuesday, at least eight large lenders, spanning state-run, private and foreign banks, held back from quoting dollar/rupee forwards in early trading, according to conversations with Reuters reporters. The reluctance stemmed from a circular from Monday night, which mandated banks to build a risk reserve for rupee derivative contracts used to hedge the currency risk on their own assets and liabilities. The circular says the margin is applicable for all rupee derivative contracts for which lenders purchase foreign currency. Bankers interpreted the provision as extending the margin requirement to interbank transactions, prompting them to reconsider quoting dollar/rupee forwards. However, a person familiar with the RBI's thinking said this interpretation was incorrect, adding that derivatives for market-making or trading were outside the scope of the circular. Three of the eight banks resumed quoting forwards following a bilateral clarification from the RBI, according to the bankers. Other currency traders said they would wait for official communication before resuming interbank quotes. With banks holding back, dollar-rupee forward volumes dropped, bid-ask spreads widened, triggering sizeable market swings. Client activity migrated to the non-deliverable forward market on concerns that onshore protection could become more expensive, a banker at a large foreign bank said. All the bankers wanted to be anonymous since they are not authorised to speak to media. INCREASED SCRUTINY OF TRADES The curbs coincide with increased scrutiny of dollar demand, the bankers said, pointing to the RBI's queries about derivative transactions on Monday. While some banks facilitating large dollar purchases received calls from the central bank, others were asked to submit client transaction details over email, the bankers said. The regulator sought granular details about client requirements, one banker at a foreign lender said. The RBI routinely engages with lenders, but the ongoing scrutiny has been more in-depth, another banker said. Despite a recent recovery, the rupee is down about 6% this year, lagging behind most Asian peers, due to pressure from high crude prices and capital outflows. MUFG, which expects the rupee to gradually fall to 97.50 by the September quarter next year, expects more measures if the rupee were to weaken further. "Ultimately for the underlying pressure on rupee to ease, this would require changes in underlying fundamental flows in India," Michael Wan, senior currency analyst at MUFG, said in a note.

item.title: AI caution favours old-school data centre builder
item.description: DayOne may raise $5 bln in a US debut as it races to tap into booming Asian demand. Like neocloud Firmus, which nixed its listing, customer concentration and a construction backlog are red flags. But DayOne's track record plus firmer delivery dates put it on more solid footing.
item.dc:creator: Robyn Mak
item.content:encoded: Factories, even for artificial intelligence, need not be complicated. Take Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers, which constructs and leases out such buildings to cloud computing providers and AI firms. Its straightforward business model, track record and firm delivery times are a contrast to upstart neocloud Firmus Technologies, which last week abandoned its listing on weak investor demand. That puts DayOne's upcoming US IPO on more solid footing. The company, which is [USN:L4N45R1CA TEXT:"looking"] to raise $5 billion at a $20 billion valuation, used to be the international arm of China's $6 billion GDS (9698.HK) before it separated and rebranded. That helps explain how it already touts a foothold in the so-called SIJORI hub - a massive cluster of data centres spanning Malaysia, Indonesia, and Singapore. The company's capacity there topped 862 megawatts as of September and is set to almost double. To compare, Australia's Firmus has just 42 megawatts of its hoped-for 1 gigawatt of capacity up and running. True, both are exposed to similar risks. Revenue concentration, for instance, is a major red flag. Almost all of Firmus' $13 billion of projected revenue comes from just two companies, AFR reported in April. Meanwhile, DayOne depends on one customer - most likely China's ByteDance, based on descriptions of the client in its prospectus - for 69% of its first-half sales. The TikTok-owner's Chinese roots add another layer of uncertainty: US legislation to restrict companies from the People's Republic from accessing high-end chips via overseas data centres is currently making its way through Washington. Losing its top AI customer could be catastrophic for DayOne, which has yet to turn a profit. But US titans may be more than happy to take its place: Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Oracle (ORCL.N) are aggressively expanding in Asia, with committed investments topping $160 billion between January 2024 and May 2026, McKinsey estimates . That's due to booming demand in the region for not only AI but also traditional computing and storage services. Crucially, DayOne is confident that it can fund and deliver substantially all of the 2.3 gigawatts of capacity committed by customers by 2028. The Company says it can construct a data centre within 12 months and for up to 30% cheaper than the industry average. Indeed, the words "faster and cheaper" may resonate with investors far more than grand ambitions like those of Firmus. Follow Robyn Mak on X . Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers on October 6 filed for a New York initial public offering. The company may seek to raise as much as $5 billion at a $20 billion valuation, Reuters reported in February. DayOne had 962 megawatts of capacity in service as of September 20, 2026, and is actively constructing an additional 962 MW of capacity across six markets, according to its prospectus. For the six months ended June 30, revenue was $512 million, compared to $151.5 million a year ago. Malaysia accounted for 87% of the total, while its top two customers accounted for 84.3% of the total. The company also said its top customer is a "global technology company with a leading short-form video platform serving a worldwide audience". China's ByteDance and Oracle are DayOne's top two customers, research group SemiAnalysis said in June 2025. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Late offense sends Guardians to ALCS Game 1 win over Rays
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Cleveland Guardians made up for a slow start by racing to a strong finish in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Cleveland Guardians made up for a slow start by racing to a strong finish in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series. Nathaniel Lowe ripped a tiebreaking two-run single in the eighth inning, lifting the Guardians to a 7-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Monday. The Guardians scored seven runs over the final four innings and finished with 14 hits in the series opener. Cleveland has erupted for 25 runs in three road contests in the playoffs heading into Game 2 on Tuesday in St. Petersburg. With the game tied at 2-2, Jose Ramirez reached on an infield single to lead off the eighth against Tyler Wells (0-1). Ramirez advanced to third base on a double from rookie Chase DeLauter. One out later, Lowe plated both with a line-drive single to center field on an 0-2 pitch from Ian Seymour. Ramirez drove in a run in the ninth inning, giving him four straight playoff games with an RBI -- tied for the longest postseason streak in franchise history with Sandy Alomar (1997) and Jim Thome (1998-99). "Cleveland is everything to me," Ramirez told TNT Sports through an interpreter. "When nobody wanted to give me a chance, they gave me a chance. This is the place I love, and they love me back." Ramirez joined DeLauter in collecting three hits apiece. Both players scored on Jo Adell's two-run double in the ninth, helping Cleveland hand Tampa Bay its first loss since a 7-3 setback to the Philadelphia Phillies on Sept. 27. "It's been a while since we've lost," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "That's a good thing. I know the guys will come back and respond tomorrow." The late uprising made a winner out of Hunter Gaddis (1-0), who allowed one hit over one scoreless inning. The Cleveland bullpen delivered five innings of one-run ball. DeLauter homered to lead off the sixth inning and Patrick Bailey did the same in the seventh for the Guardians, who have won four in a row since facing an 0-2 deficit against the Chicago White Sox in the AL Division Series. "I think we have a ton of momentum right now. I think we're playing good baseball," Cade Smith, who retired the side in order in the ninth inning on Monday, told SiriusXM. "I just hope we carry that into tomorrow." Cedric Mullins belted a solo homer in the eighth inning and Junior Caminero and Jonny DeLuca each had an RBI single for Tampa Bay. Wells permitted two runs on two hits in one-third of an inning while pitching in a game for the first time since Sept. 12. Tampa Bay got off to a fast start against Guardians starter Foster Griffin, recording four hits in the first inning to take a 2-0 lead. Yandy Diaz doubled to lead off the inning. He advanced to third base on a sacrifice bunt and scored on Caminero's RBI single to left-center field. Caminero moved to second base on a two-out single by Victor Mesa Jr. and scored on DeLuca's single to center field. In the sixth, DeLauter halved the deficit by depositing a first-pitch fastball from Drew Rasmussen over the wall in left-center field. The homer was the first of DeLauter's postseason career. Bailey forged a 2-2 tie after sending a first-pitch cutter from Rasmussen over the wall in center field. Bailey's second homer in his last three games sent Rasmussen to the showers. Rasmussen allowed two runs on eight hits and no walks in six-plus innings. He struck out seven. Griffin yielded two runs on five hits in four innings. He fanned three without issuing a walk. --Field Level Media

item.title: IMF cites AI slowdown, spiking yields as looming global market risks
item.description: The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing risks from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff, rising government bond yields, or cyberattacks as potential threats facing still-resilient markets.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder, Selena Li
item.content:encoded: The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing risks from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff, rising government bond yields, or cyberattacks as potential threats facing still-resilient markets. The IMF said in its Global Financial Stability Report that AI investments have so far [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"helped offset"] economic drags from war in the Middle East and overall policy uncertainty. But it noted "growing evidence" that AI capabilities may not require as much investment, or the potential economic gains may not be as large as expected. "An AI market correction will affect the real economy," Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director in the IMF's Monetary and Capital Markets Department, said at a press briefing in Bangkok. He said while global risk sentiment was very strong, underpinned by solid earnings and optimism about AI, such "resilience is not necessarily safety". An AI correction would have impacts on wealth and investment that could spill into broader markets, he said. The risk of such a selloff, as well as a spike in sovereign bond yields or a major cyberattack, were among "plausible near-term catalysts" that policymakers should monitor, the IMF said in its report. While each of these risks might be manageable on its own, they also could trigger vulnerabilities with potential systemic implications, Vamvakidis said. Should the momentum in AI investment slow, the IMF noted growing leverage in the sector could exacerbate any shock by triggering forced selling and higher volatility. For example, hyperscalers now represent 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, up from less than 1% in 2024. "The consequences of an AI correction could be global," the IMF warned, as it called on policymakers to curb leverage use, including derivatives and margin loans, where it is "excessive." RISING YIELDS The IMF said bond market risks have worsened since [USN:L6N40W0X6 TEXT:"its April report"], as higher energy prices have driven [USN:L1N45U12M TEXT:"government bond yields up"]. Historically high sovereign debt levels and unresolved fiscal deficits in major economies were adding to the pressure. "The market is concerned about absorption potential of the huge issuance that is coming from the sovereigns and increasingly also from the private sector, at the time that central banks are shrinking their balances, and we have to rely more on price-sensitive investors," Vamvakidis said. The IMF report said bond markets have so far dealt with the stress well, with hedge funds able to unwind some of their repurchase agreement borrowing without triggering turmoil in repo markets. The group called on policymakers to put public debt on a sustainable path. On cyber threats, the IMF said that a lack of resources, particularly in emerging markets, and a growing reliance on a small number of critical providers was making [USN:L6N43I17J TEXT:"cyber defense more difficult"]. In over 70% of cases so far in 2026, software providers have had almost no time to patch vulnerabilities before they were exploited, a 20 percentage point jump from a year ago, the IMF said. It noted that while AI can help address some of these risks, models were also making cyberattacks more sophisticated. The IMF cautioned that a major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence, which could quickly ripple throughout markets. It called on policymakers to boost cybersecurity capacity, including stricter oversight of third-party technology vendors. The IMF said its stress test models showed banks' capital cushions remained robust even in a hypothetical downturn triggered by an AI slowdown and bond market fragility. But it warned of "pockets of weakness," with banks representing 22% of global banking assets found to have "weak" capital levels under the test, up from 18% under the 2025 test.

item.title: Wild make first-period flurry hold up in win over Golden Knights
item.description: Danila Yurov scored to finish off a first-period flurry for the Minnesota Wild, who held on for a 4-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights on Monday evening in Saint Paul, Minn.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Danila Yurov scored to finish off a first-period flurry for the Minnesota Wild, who held on for a 4-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights on Monday evening in Saint Paul, Minn. Matt Boldy and Maxim Shabanov also scored in the first period for Minnesota, which won its second game in a row. Joel Eriksson Ek added an empty-net goal. Rasmus Andersson and William Karlsson scored one goal apiece for Vegas, which never led. The Golden Knights lost for the first time in their past five games. Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 21 of 23 shots in the win. Golden Knights goaltender Carter Hart allowed three goals on 27 shots. The Wild opened the scoring with 8:10 to go in the first period. Boldy blasted a one-timer that Hart denied, but the rebound came back to Boldy's stick, leading to a successful second-chance snap shot. Less than three minutes later, Shabanov scored on the power play to increase the Wild's advantage to 2-0. Shabanov fired a wrist shot from the top of the left circle, and the puck hit off Hart's blocker and ricocheted into the net. Minnesota made it 3-0 two-plus minutes after that, which concluded a three-goal stretch within 5:07 in the back half of the first period. Bobby Brink zipped a pinpoint pass to the slot for Yurov, who buried a one-timer. Vegas got on the scoreboard with 17:23 left in the second period. Andersson steadied the puck and fired a long-range slap shot from near the blue line for his first goal. The Golden Knights cut the deficit to 3-2 with 10:35 remaining in the third period. On a two-on-one rush, Brett Howden flipped a saucer pass to Karlsson, who finished the job with a one-timer. Vegas pulled its goaltender for an extra attacker in the final two minutes, but Minnesota held firm. Eriksson Ek scored an empty-net goal to make it 4-2 with 1:22 to go. Wild forward Nico Sturm left the game in the first period and did not return after taking a puck to the right side of his head. Sturm was battling for position near the net when a teammate's wrist shot struck him near the helmet. --Field Level Media

item.title: India's widened FX curbs, RBI intervention lift rupee to one-month peak
item.description: The Indian rupee rose to its strongest level in a month on Tuesday, hoisted by fresh central bank measures to alleviate pressure on the Asian currency and likely spot market intervention that magnified their impact.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee rose to its strongest level in a month on Tuesday, hoisted by [USN:L4N45Z04K TEXT:"fresh central bank measures"] to alleviate pressure on the Asian currency and likely spot market intervention that magnified their impact. The rupee rose to 95.0725 in early trading, the highest since early September, before paring gains to trade higher by 0.5% at 95.25 per dollar. The Reserve Bank of India on Monday widened the scope of a recent cash deposit mandate for FX hedges to cover all transactions by banks, including hedging of the lenders' assets and liabilities. This was the latest in a slew of steps since Saturday aimed at supporting the rupee, which last week tested record lows amid pressure from high oil prices and capital outflows. The latest change, however, has [USN:L4N45Z09Q TEXT:"sowed confusion"] among bankers and prompted some of them to stop quoting dollar-rupee forwards in the interbank market. Multiple bankers characterised the morning trading as "nervous," following the salvo of regulatory steps. State-run banks, meanwhile, were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, traders said. "The repeated rejection of 96.70–96.90 suggests that the dollar is facing a significant ceiling. With the RBI’s measures supporting the rupee, we expect USD/INR to move towards 95.00–94.80 in the near term," said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex in Mumbai. The dollar-rupee forward market saw sharp swings with far-tenor premiums moving between gains and losses. Traders also pointed to sharp moves in the non-deliverable forward market. The USD/INR 1-year forward implied yield, for instance, swung between 3.62% and 4.02% against 3.83% at the previous close.

item.title: AI boom bolstered growth in global trade, benefiting China and India, IMF says
item.description: The strong demand for AI has bolstered growth in China, India and other Asian countries and outpaced the overall growth in global trade, the IMF's new chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The strong demand for AI has bolstered growth in China, India and other Asian countries and outpaced the overall growth in global trade, the IMF's new chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said on Tuesday. Global trade would have grown at a far slower rate without the AI boost, Tenreyro told reporters at the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok. A long-time professor at the London School of Economics, [USN:FWN4390JA TEXT:"Tenreyro started her new job"] at the IMF in August. Tenreyro said the IMF remained concerned about high debt levels, urging countries to start cutting budgets to reduce deficits. She said central bankers should pursue more restrictive policies, including raising interest rates to get inflation rates back to target. Tenreyro said the AI-related boom in investment and trade had been a key driver of global growth, but AI supply chains were highly concentrated in a few countries and sectors, which created potential chokepoints. Global trade grew 8.3% between 2023 and 2025, while global trade in AI grew by 29%, she said. Without the AI trade, overall growth in trade would have been only 4.6%. The IMF flagged that a market value correction and AI threats to cybersecurity could also weigh on growth and add to financial stability risks. Tenreyro said the IMF's baseline forecast assumed the AI boom would dissipate over time, but another scenario showed that actual productivity gains from a prolonged AI boom could limit its inflationary impact. If the AI boom persisted but did not result in productivity gains, the gains for growth would be smaller and inflation would be higher, she said. And a reassessment of the profitability gains from AI would result in downward adjustment in demand. "It's basically an unwind of this boom that we are seeing," Tenreyro said, adding that the IMF was updating its research on the impact of AI on jobs.

item.title: Gold ticks up as oil eases; spotlight on US inflation data
item.description: Gold ticked up on Tuesday as oil prices slipped, while markets focused on the upcoming US inflation data for fresh signals on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory.
item.dc:creator: Ashitha Shivaprasad
item.content:encoded: Gold ticked up on Tuesday as oil prices slipped, while markets focused on the upcoming US inflation data for fresh signals on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory. Spot gold was up 0.4% to $4,188.27 per ounce by 06:24 GMT after hitting a one-week peak on Monday. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.5% to $4,212.50 per ounce. Oil prices fell and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week. Higher oil prices, driven by Middle East tensions, have raised inflation concerns and strengthened the case for restrictive monetary policy. While gold is considered a hedge against inflation, higher rates often push investors toward yield-bearing assets rather than the non-yielding metal. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is due on Wednesday, and the Producer Price Index (PPI) report is scheduled for Thursday. "US CPI data will be critical for gold in the short term," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. If inflation comes in hotter than expected, particularly on the core measure, and prompts even a modest increase in expectations of an October rate hike, it could result in another dip in gold, he added. Currently, traders see only a 19% chance of a Fed rate hike this month but are pricing in an 85% chance of a December increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool. Cleveland Fed President [USN:S0N44V02D TEXT:"Beth Hammack"] said the US central bank should move "relatively quickly" to a more restrictive monetary policy stance to control inflation, which she feels has become broader-based and is starting to influence firms' price-setting plans. On the geopolitical front, [USN:L6N45Y0OR TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"] said it was facing a new barrage of incoming fire and that Riyadh airport would remain shut for now, days after Saturday's deadly missile strike on a departure terminal that was claimed by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis. Among other metals, spot silver gained 0.2% to $60.46 per ounce, platinum 0.5% to $1,694.65, and palladium fell 0.2% to $1,141.23 per ounce.

item.title: AI investment props up global growth, but war and debt threaten outlook, IMF says
item.description: The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East , but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday. Despite a more protracted conflict that has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, the IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1%, a slight uptick from the 3.0% it [USN:L1N43A0MP TEXT:"predicted in July"]. The [USN:L1N45Y0HP TEXT:"World Economic Outlook"] forecast, released as global economic and finance leaders gather in Bangkok for the [USN:L1N45X02O TEXT:"IMF and World Bank annual meetings"], is about even with the [USN:L1N40X0Q2 TEXT:"most optimistic scenario"] issued in April but below 2025 global growth of 3.5%. For 2027, the IMF predicts 3.4% global growth, flat with the July forecast and up 0.2 percentage point from April. The slight improvement is largely due to continued strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure, prompting growth upgrades for key advanced economies building AI platforms and especially for countries supplying AI hardware, including South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico and Thailand, which is hosting the meetings this week. "The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits, so we need to move from just coping to rebuilding," the IMF's chief economist, Silvana Tenreyro, told a news conference. "We need to restore fiscal space. We need to rebuild supply-side resilience." She said major downside risks to growth include a prolonged, intensified war in the Middle East that spikes inflation pressures, rising bond yields that raise government borrowing costs, El Nino-driven extreme weather events and a reassessment of AI profitability that craters investment and asset prices. Countries and companies moved quickly to mitigate the oil price shock, drawing down reserves, substituting other suppliers and energy sources and cutting oil demand, Petya Koeva Brooks, the IMF's deputy research director, told Reuters in a separate interview. She said global growth would have fallen to 2.5% this year without these measures, but their effect is fading as the war drags on. The IMF noted a growing divergence between countries benefiting from AI and those bypassed by it. Just 32 countries now account for 95% of global growth, compared to 54 countries in April. Downward growth revisions have become more widespread, with the IMF downgrading 47% of economies since the April forecasts were issued, including several energy importers outside AI value chains. Hardest hit by downgrades were the Gulf countries directly impacted by the US-Israeli war against Iran, with Saudi Arabia's GDP now forecast to contract 3.3% this year compared with the 1.7% growth predicted in July. Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are also expected to fall into deep recessions, with 2026 contractions of 7.6%, 16%, 16.7%, 15.6% and 3.9%, respectively. UNITED STATES FLAT, IMPROVEMENT IN EUROPE Among major economies, the IMF forecast US growth of 2.3% for both 2026 and 2027, unchanged for this year and 0.1 percentage point higher for next year. The US economy is expected to be supported by robust private consumption, tax cuts and AI investment, though the boost from AI will be offset by its large import content. Euro zone growth for 2026 was upgraded to 1.1% from 0.9% in July due to stronger investment in AI, participation in AI value chains such as chemical production in Germany, and higher defense spending in EU countries. Britain's 2026 growth forecast also was upgraded by 0.3 percentage point from July to 1.3% due to larger AI investment. The IMF forecast China's growth at 4.5% for 2026 and 4.0% for 2027, both down 0.1 percentage point from July, as higher oil prices exacerbate weak domestic demand despite strong exports. India remains the world's fastest-growing major economy at 7.0% for both 2026 and 2027, up 0.6 percentage point this year and 0.3 percentage point next year compared with the July forecasts amid robust domestic demand, services activity and AI investment. The AI investment surge is projected to keep upward pressure on prices, with global headline consumer price inflation forecast at 4.7% in 2026 and 4.1% for 2027. ENERGY PRICE, AI RISKS Participants at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok will be assessing a precarious outlook. The IMF forecasts are based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen in March 2027 with a broad return to pre-war shipping conditions occurring by October 2027. The IMF assumes an average oil price of $96 per barrel for 2026 and $87 in 2027. But under an adverse scenario highlighted in the report, in which a worsening war pushes oil prices to $130 per barrel through the first quarter of 2027, growth would be reduced by 0.2 percentage point in 2026 and 0.5 percentage point in 2027. Inflation in 2027 would surge by another 1.1 percentage point to 5.2%. AI is also a huge source of uncertainty, with major downside and upside risks, the IMF report said. Under a scenario of faster adoption of the technology and accelerated investment, global GDP could rise a further 0.6% by 2029, with the bulk of the benefits going to the US and China. But if productivity gains from AI fail to materialize, prompting a sharp decline in investment, US GDP could fall by 0.8% directly, causing spillovers to Asian technology exporters with a total direct GDP impact of as much as 0.4% by 2028. This shift would also trigger a sharp reduction in asset prices and tighter financial conditions that cause a major drop in consumption, particularly in the US, the IMF said. Higher global bond yields would further reduce activity, with a combined global output reduction of 1.1% by 2028, including a 1.8% drop in US output. The IMF also warned that elevated public debt levels, particularly in advanced economies, increase the risk of sharply higher borrowing costs that can weigh on growth prospects. It urged governments to stop delaying action to rebuild fiscal buffers and articulate credible medium-term plans to bring debt back to sustainable levels — advice that IMF officials [USN:L6N45T0FB TEXT:"plan to push"] at the Bangkok meetings.

item.title: US says it opposes Chinese 'coercion', after Belize, Paraguay ministers sanctioned
item.description: The Trump administration opposes "coercion and aggression" by China against countries for exercising their sovereign rights, the US State Department said, after Beijing sanctioned Belizean and Paraguayan ministers over their ties to Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration opposes "coercion and aggression" by China against countries for exercising their sovereign rights, the US State Department said, after Beijing [USN:L1N45Y01O TEXT:"sanctioned"] Belizean and Paraguayan ministers over their ties to Taiwan. Paraguay and Belize are two of just 12 countries to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China says Taiwan is one of its provinces with no right to behave like a state, a view Taipei's government strongly rejects. The sanctions are largely symbolic because ministers from Taiwan's diplomatic allies generally do not travel to China. Beijing has previously imposed similar measures mainly on Western politicians for their support of democratically governed Taiwan. "The Trump administration opposes coercion and aggression by China against countries in our hemisphere for exercising their sovereign rights," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement. Pigott cited previous comments by Secretary of State Marco Rubio that the US "will not allow our region to become a base of operation for adversaries, competitors, and rivals to threaten our security or undermine our partnerships". "We stand with our friends and partners, including Taiwan, to advance our shared prosperity, security, and values," Pigott added. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said the United States should "stop sending the wrong signals to Taiwan separatist forces". The United States is Taiwan's most important international backer, despite the lack of formal diplomatic ties. Washington has been concerned not only by Beijing's efforts to win over Taiwan's remaining allies, but also by attempts to increase its influence in Latin America. TAIWAN'S VISIBILITY 'GROWING HIGHER' Speaking on Tuesday to reporters at parliament in Taipei, Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi said China was extending "transnational repression" to Taiwan's allies. "Taiwan's international visibility is growing higher and higher, and they will be kept busy by this fact," Chen said, referring to China. "Do they plan to sanction the whole world?" Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai said Beijing had no right to interfere in the domestic affairs of, or influence the diplomacy of, any sovereign and independent state, "including the Republic of China", referring to the island's formal name. "At the same time, we will resist any expansion of hegemony or authoritarianism," he added, also speaking at parliament. China has stepped up pressure on Taiwan's remaining diplomatic allies to sever ties with Taipei. The last country to do so was the tiny Pacific Island nation of Nauru, in 2024. Honduras ended its decades-long ties with Taiwan in 2023.

item.title: Linus Ullmark shines as Senators turn back Devils
item.description: Linus Ullmark continued his early-season dominance to carry the Ottawa Senators to their third consecutive victory with a 4-1 win over the New Jersey Devils Monday night in Newark, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Linus Ullmark continued his early-season dominance to carry the Ottawa Senators to their third consecutive victory with a 4-1 win over the New Jersey Devils Monday night in Newark, N.J. Ullmark impressed with 29 saves to lift his record to a perfect 5-0-0 to start the season. Tim Stutzle scored and picked up an assist, while Shane Pinto, Stephen Halliday and Tyler Kleven also lit the lamp for the Senators. Arseny Gritsyuk tallied the Devils' lone goal and Nico Daws finished with 16 saves in the losing effort. The Devils' physical play in the early going finally caught up to them as Anthony Mantha delivered a dangerous check on Nikolas Matinpalo that drew a five-minute major just over halfway through the opening frame. Matinpalo was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest with an upper-body injury. Fabian Zetterlund had the Senators' only real chance to score during their extended man advantage, but Daws slid across to deny the one-timer opportunity. Ottawa started the second period off with a bang as Pinto found the back of the net just nine seconds in to give the Senators the 1-0 lead. Michael Amadio picked up a pass from Claude Giroux and relayed it over to Pinto for his first goal of the season. After failing to convert on their first four opportunities, the Senators finally found some power-play success as Stutzle spotted Halliday open in front of the net to double up the lead with 11:20 remaining in the second. Stutzle picked up his 10th point of the season when he tipped Thomas Chabot's point shot past Daws to make it 3-0 with 8:50 left in the contest. The Devils thought they finally got one past Ullmark less than a minute later, but it was ruled that Cody Glass illegally poked it loose from underneath the Senators' netminder following a successful coach's challenge. Gritsyuk spoiled Ullmark's shutout bid as his shot passed through a screen and into the back of the net with just 5:01 remaining. Kleven locked up the victory with an empty-net goal. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tencent experiences strong demand for $4.5 billion debt sale, defying AI scrutiny
item.description: Tencent Holdings has received investor demand worth more than three times the Chinese tech giant's plan to raise at least $4.5 billion via US dollar and offshore Chinese yuan debt offerings, even as AI spending jitters hit the global markets.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Ankur Banerjee
item.content:encoded: Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) has received investor demand worth more than three times the Chinese tech giant's plan to raise at least $4.5 billion via US dollar and offshore Chinese yuan debt offerings, even as AI spending jitters hit the global markets. Tencent plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, according to the deal term sheet, and the latest borrowing comes as the company increases investment in AI infrastructure and products. The latest debt sale comes amid technology firms globally [USN:L6N45F1AU TEXT:"raising billions of dollars"] to finance [USN:L1N455022 TEXT:"AI investment"]s, although investors have become [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"more selective about companies"] funding costly AI infrastructure amid elevated borrowing costs. Shares in AI suppliers came under [USN:L1N45Z029 TEXT:"heavy selling pressure"] on Tuesday on growing concerns about competition risks in the sector and rising interest rates weighing on AI-related borrowing and a spending spree. Despite those concerns, investor demand for Tencent's 10-year and 20-year US dollar notes topped $4 billion, including $921 million in interest from the joint lead managers, according to an updated term sheet issued on Tuesday. Order books for the 10-year and 30-year offshore yuan, or dim sum, bonds exceeded 77 billion yuan ($11.5 billion), the sheet showed. The total demand worth $15.5 billion is significantly higher than at least [USN:L4N45Y01K TEXT:"$4.5 billion"] that a person with direct knowledge of the deal told Reuters on Monday the company was looking to raise. The company [USN:L1N42H00X TEXT:"last tapped the bond market in June"], raising about $4.66 billion through dollar- and yuan-denominated notes. Its return to the bond market so quickly suggests capital remains available for AI, particularly for companies with strong cash flows, balance sheets and credible monetisation plans, said Allspring Global Investments portfolio manager Gary Tan. "We are seeing a more definitive shift in sentiment around the pace of AI spending, as investors increasingly view financing availability and the cost of capital as potential bottlenecks to a further acceleration in AI investment," he said. Tencent has not responded to a Reuters request seeking comment on its debt issuance. The deal term sheet did not specify how much the company is looking to raise via the sale of US dollar and offshore yuan notes. CAPITAL EXPENDITURE DOUBLES Shares in Tencent were down 0.5% on Tuesday, underperforming the benchmark Hang Seng Index (.HSI) that climbed 0.1%. The Hang Seng Tech Index (.HSTECH) fell nearly 1%. Tencent's shares have fallen about 30% so far this year. Tencent set initial guidance for the 10-year dollar notes at about 115 basis points over comparable US Treasury bonds. The 20-year notes were set at about 140 basis points over Treasuries, according to the term sheet. It set initial yield guidance at around 2.90% for the 10-year offshore yuan notes and 3.50% for the 30-year notes, the sheets showed. The final coupons for all the bonds are expected to be determined later Tuesday, according to the sheets. Tencent's capital expenditure more than doubled to 96.3 billion yuan in the first half of 2026 from 45.9 billion yuan a year earlier, according to its offering documents. The spending included computing equipment, software and data centres. The bonds are expected to be rated A1 by Moody's and A+ by S&P. Tencent is rated A1 by Moody's, A+ by S&P and A by Fitch, according to the term sheet. JPMorgan (JPM.N) , Goldman Sachs (GS.N) , HSBC (HSBA.L) and Morgan Stanley (MS.N) are joint global coordinators for Tencent's dollar bond offering, the sheet showed. ICBC (Asia), Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of China, Bank of Communications, China Construction Bank, CITIC Securities, HSBC and JPMorgan are coordinating the offshore yuan sale, according to the sheet. ($1 = 6.6923 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Oil falls as Russian diesel supply prospects counter Gulf supply risks
item.description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week, as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.
item.dc:creator: Anjana Anil, Trixie Yap
item.content:encoded: Oil prices fell on Tuesday and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week, as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia. Brent crude futures dropped $1.18, or 1.1%, to $105.47 a barrel by 0625 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $1.17, or 1.3%, at $92.57 a barrel. Both benchmarks climbed nearly $2 a barrel in the previous session, with Brent settling at its highest since September 15. US President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"supply diesel"] to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine . Additional supplies could help alleviate tightness in global fuel markets, tempering some of the supply concerns that have supported crude prices recently. However, "there is considerable scepticism over the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, particularly with reports that Russia has hit Ukrainian energy targets since Trump announced it," ING analysts said in a note. Lawmakers from both parties in the US complained Trump's agreement with Putin appears to [USN:L1N45Y0QE TEXT:"violate US law"] barring imports of Russian energy until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine. Concerns over the vulnerability of Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping lanes remained in focus after Iran-aligned Houthis [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"struck Riyadh's international airport"] over the weekend, while [USN:L1N45T0HL TEXT:"tanker attacks"] were [USN:S8N44X01M TEXT:"reported"] near the Strait of Hormuz. The incidents threatened to derail a recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, and have reinforced fears of further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes. "Fresh diesel supply from Russia and steadier Saudi flows are offering some relief, yet the market still looks more worried about the risk of further hits to ships or pipelines in the Gulf than it is reassured by extra barrels," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade. "Until we see clearer signs of de-escalation, the path of least resistance still leans higher," he said. Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs have surged to unprecedented levels of over [USN:L4N45Y17D TEXT:"one-third"] of the commodity value, impeding efficient movement of crude oil and products. OPEC has [USN:S8N45M04R TEXT:"revised down"] its oil demand growth forecast for this year to 400,000 barrels per day from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, in line with developments throughout the year, Haitham Al Ghais, Secretary General of the organisation said on Monday.

item.title: Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeps alive BOJ rate-hike view
item.description: The data highlights mounting inflationary pressure that keeps alive market expectations of a near-term interest rate hike.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September, according to data released on Tuesday, slowing from the previous month but highlighting mounting inflationary pressure that keeps alive market expectations of a near-term interest rate hike.
